purpose: Machine-readable catalog for the Explore & Design (data-modeling) AI wizard. Lets an LLM ground its model proposals on real entity scaffolds, on the detection endpoints that are actually available, and on the two sample-data strategies (real clone vs synthetic) — without reading the UI source. Mirrors the workflow ETL catalog shape.

entity_template.label: string — human title
entity_template.description: string — what the entity is for
entity_template.typical_columns: array of { name, role, type } — the columns this entity scaffold usually carries; `role` is one of surrogate_key | natural_key | foreign_key | measure | attribute | flag | audit | scd_meta
entity_template.usage: string — when a modeler should reach for this entity

detection_strategy.endpoint: string — the explore-design API path that backs it
detection_strategy.inputs: array of string — request fields the endpoint consumes
detection_strategy.outputs: array of string — response fields the endpoint returns
detection_strategy.description: string — what the detection does and when to run it

sample_generation.label: string — human title
sample_generation.data_class: real | synthetic — real = from a connected source, synthetic = AI-fabricated
sample_generation.row_cap: number — hard maximum rows this strategy may emit (free-discovery cap)
sample_generation.endpoint: string — the API the strategy calls (null for none)
sample_generation.free_discovery: boolean — true when usage stays inside the free-discovery allowance
sample_generation.description: string — how the strategy produces rows
sample_generation.cap_rule: string — the human-readable free-discovery / metering rule

rules: `typical_columns` are conventional scaffolds — the modeler/AI may add, drop or rename; they are NOT a fixed schema.
A detection_strategy `endpoint` must match a real function in exploreDesignApi.ts — no invented endpoints.
Every sample_generation strategy is capped at FREE_DISCOVERY_ROW_CAP (1000) rows; the cap is enforced client-side regardless of what the endpoint returns.
`data_class: synthetic` rows must ALWAYS be labelled synthetic in the UI and never presented as real data.
Beyond the free-discovery cap, full-volume access is a paid-plan / metered concern handled elsewhere — this catalog only documents the cap.

categories.dimensional: Star/snowflake schema entities — dimensions, facts, junctions
categories.modeling_aid: Helper entities — bridges and pre-aggregated rollups

entity_templates.label: Dimension table
entity_templates.description: Descriptive context for facts — the 'who / what / where' of a star schema. One row per business entity, low-to-mid cardinality.
entity_templates.usage: Reach for this when columns describe an entity (customer, product, store) rather than measure an event.

entity_templates.label: Fact table
entity_templates.description: Measurable business events — high row count, narrow on attributes, wide on measures and foreign keys to dimensions.
entity_templates.usage: Reach for this when the table has >= 2 numeric measures and foreign keys pointing at dimensions.

entity_templates.label: Junction (associative) table
entity_templates.description: Resolves a many-to-many relationship between two entities. Composite key of the two foreign keys, optionally with relationship attributes.
entity_templates.usage: Reach for this when two tables relate many-to-many (e.g. orders <-> promotions).

entity_templates.label: SCD Type 1 dimension
entity_templates.description: Slowly-changing dimension that OVERWRITES on change — no history retained. Simplest history strategy.
entity_templates.usage: Use when historical attribute values are not needed and the latest value is sufficient.

entity_templates.label: SCD Type 2 dimension
entity_templates.description: Slowly-changing dimension that retains full history — a new row per attribute change, with effective-dating and a current-row flag.
entity_templates.usage: Use when point-in-time reporting requires the attribute values as they were on a past date.

entity_templates.label: Bridge table
entity_templates.description: Resolves a hierarchical or multi-valued dimension relationship (e.g. an account belonging to several segments), often with an allocation weight.
entity_templates.usage: Use for variable-depth hierarchies or multi-valued dimension memberships where a junction is not enough.

entity_templates.label: Aggregate (rollup) table
entity_templates.description: Pre-summarized fact data at a coarser grain — trades storage for query speed on common rollups.
entity_templates.usage: Use when a heavy fact is repeatedly queried at a fixed coarse grain (daily-by-store, monthly-by-region).

detection_strategies.description: Reads true column data types, row count and per-column statistics from a connected source. The basis for distinguishing a connected source (row_count > 0) from a no-source path.
AI semantic classification of each column (KEY / METRIC / DIMENSION / AUDIT / PII). Falls back to a name-based heuristic when Cortex is unreachable.
Detects foreign-key relationships across the selected table set. Falls back to a name-match heuristic when Cortex is unreachable.

outputs: columns flagged isPrimaryKey from KEY-category columns whose name looks like a key
detection_strategies.description: Primary-key candidates are derived from the classify-columns KEY category combined with a name heuristic (id / *_id / *_key / *_pk). No standalone endpoint — it is a projection over classification + profile.

sample_generation.label: Clone from connected source
sample_generation.description: Pulls real rows from a connected source via tablePreview with limit=1000. The genuine free-discovery sample — lets a user explore the actual data shape before committing to a paid plan.
sample_generation.cap_rule: Capped at 1000 rows. The preview endpoint is called with limit=1000 and the response is additionally sliced to 1000 client-side. Beyond 1000 rows, full-volume access requires a paid plan.

sample_generation.label: LLM synthetic sample
sample_generation.description: Fabricates rows with the LLM when NO source is connected. Rows are generated to match the declared/expected schema. Always labelled synthetic — never presented as real data.
sample_generation.cap_rule: Hard-capped at 1000 rows client-side. The LLM is prompted for a smaller batch (the 15s Cortex budget cannot emit 1000 rows); whatever it returns is parsed, repaired and sliced to <= 1000. Synthetic rows never count against real-data metering.

samples.title: Sample 1 — Retail star schema
samples.summary: A classic sales star: one fact surrounded by three dimensions.

entities.name: fct_sales
entities.grain: one row per sales line item

samples.sample_generation: clone_from_source when the retail source is connected; otherwise llm_synthetic seeded from the declared columns.

samples.title: Sample 2 — Customer sentiment model
samples.summary: A fact of review events plus a junction resolving reviews-to-topics many-to-many.
samples.sample_generation: llm_synthetic — sentiment text is fabricated by the LLM and clearly badged synthetic so QA never mistakes it for production reviews.

samples.title: Sample 3 — Aggregate rollup over a fact
samples.summary: A daily-by-store aggregate table derived from the retail fact for fast dashboards.

entities.name: agg_sales_daily_store
entities.grain: one row per day per store

samples.sample_generation: clone_from_source — the rollup is small enough that the real 1000-row free-discovery sample shows the full table.
